sections.html:
Bossier City lies on the Red River's east bank in Bossier Parish, facing Shreveport. Both cities belong to one metro area. The 2020 count was 62,701 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 63,259, spread over 43.80 square miles of land. Interstate 20, Interstate 220 and US Route 80 are the main roads, and Arthur Ray Teague Parkway and the Bossier Strip are common landmarks in listings.

Casino resorts line the river, including Margaritaville, Horseshoe and Boomtown. The Cyber Innovation Center and its National Cyber Research Park draw technology employers, and the parish runs its own community college. Hospitality, defense and technology jobs bring different kinds of buyers and tenants.

For 2020 to 2024, 53.2 percent of housing units are owner-occupied and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $202,100. Treat both as citywide averages, not a quote for your house.

Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,462 with a mortgage and $412 without one. Median gross rent is $1,107, and the city has 25,926 households.

At that rent level, many local owners keep a house as a rental. A landlord with a month to month tenant can get out more easily than one whose fixed term runs beyond the planned closing, so check lease dates first. If a tenant will stay, ask a buyer early whether they want the lease, and give the tenant proper notice about showings.

sections.h2: How much does Barksdale Air Force Base shape the market?
sections.html:
Barksdale Air Force Base is the biggest single driver of turnover in Bossier City housing. It is home to the 2d Bomb Wing, described by the Air Force as its largest bomb wing, along with Air Force Global Strike Command and Eighth Air Force. The base supports nearly 9,000 active-duty, Reserve and civilian workers plus 6,000 dependents, maintains about 1,000 houses on base, and reported a $980 million economic impact for 2023.

Military orders create two kinds of sellers:

  • Owners with short permanent change of station orders who cannot wait on a buyer's loan.
  • Owners who moved away, now manage a rental from a distance, and decide to sell after a bad vacancy or repair bill.

For both, a firm closing date usually beats top dollar, so settle that priority before choosing how to sell.

Expect a humid climate here, with roughly 51 inches of rain a year, hot summers and the occasional hard freeze. The nearest long-record station, Shreveport Regional Airport, shows 51.41 inches of average precipitation, 101.2 days with measurable rain and 1.4 inches of snow a year, with a record high of 110 degrees in August and a record low of minus 5 degrees in February. Air conditioning runs hard for months, and a freeze can crack exposed pipes, so inspectors look closely at HVAC, attics and plumbing in unheated spaces.

  • Keep roof invoices handy, since summer heat is hard on roofs and attic ventilation.
  • Homes near the Red River or its bayous should have a current flood zone determination ready.
  • Older houses may have galvanized plumbing or aging electrical panels that lenders flag.

Print the FEMA flood map for your parcel before listing, since flood status is usually the first thing a buyer asks about.

The city's Property Standards and Code Enforcement Division handles basic upkeep rules for private property. Reports of violations should include as much detail as possible. Unincorporated parts of the parish fall under a separate Property Standards department run by the Bossier Parish Police Jury, so who you call depends on whether the address is inside the city. City ordinances are posted in the Municode library.

Inherited or vacant house? Walk the lot before listing. Tall grass, broken fencing and debris draw the usual complaints, and clearing them can stop a complaint from becoming a lien or a delayed closing.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Bossier Parish Clerk of Court
sections.html:
Sale deeds are recorded by the clerk. Fees for a conveyance or mortgage document start at $105 for one to five pages, which covers indexing up to 10 names, one certified copy and the state portal fee.

Document lengthRecording fee
1 to 5 pages$105
6 to 25 pages$205
26 to 50 pages$305
Over 50 pages$305 plus $5 per extra page
Cancellation$55

A document filed in both the mortgage and conveyance records is charged for each. Louisiana law requires a sale of an immovable to be made by authentic act or by act under private signature, so you sign before a notary and the deed is then recorded here. Call the clerk to confirm the current schedule before closing. Your notary will usually collect the recording charge at the table, so ask for the exact figure ahead of time and confirm who is paying it under your purchase agreement.

sections.h2: How a Bossier City sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the notary or closing attorney starts a title search and requests your mortgage payoff. Have your deed, latest tax bill and any lease ready. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection to the timeline, while a cash buyer can often close as soon as the title work is done.

You sign the act of sale in front of the notary, and the deed then goes to the Bossier Parish Clerk of Court. Your loan balance, unpaid taxes and recording charges are subtracted from what you receive. Ask the notary for the settlement figures a few days ahead, and raise any odd line item before signing day. If the buyer is paying cash, the lender steps drop out, though the title search and recording still happen.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Bossier City house?
sections.html:
Timing, condition and tenants decide the best route. Listing exposes the house to more buyers. A cash sale tends to be faster and asks for fewer repairs.

  • A military or relocating owner may want a closing date that matches orders.
  • A landlord with a damaged unit may prefer to sell as-is rather than fund repairs.
  • An heir managing an out-of-state estate may want one signing rather than many showings.

Whichever route you pick, read the contract and cancellation terms before you sign.

Before you talk to any buyer, write down your lowest acceptable net after the loan payoff, taxes and closing costs. That single number makes it much easier to compare a listing that might take months against a cash offer that closes on a date you choose, and it keeps you from agreeing to terms that leave you short.

faqs.q: Is Bossier City part of Shreveport?
faqs.a: No. Bossier City is a separate city in Bossier Parish on the east bank of the Red River, across from Shreveport in Caddo Parish. The two share one metro area and many employers.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Bossier City house?
faqs.a: The Bossier Parish Clerk of Court records conveyance and mortgage documents. The fee is $105 for one to five pages, which includes indexing up to 10 names, a certified copy and the portal fee.

faqs.q: How many Bossier City homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: About 53.2 percent for 2020 to 2024, with a median home value of $202,100. Those are citywide figures and will not match any single house.

faqs.q: Who enforces property maintenance in Bossier City?
faqs.a: The Property Standards and Code Enforcement Division handles private property inside the city. Unincorporated areas go to the Bossier Parish Police Jury's Property Standards department.

faqs.q: Does Barksdale affect selling a house in Bossier City?
faqs.a: It can. The base supports nearly 9,000 workers and had a reported $980 million economic impact in 2023, so military moves create regular turnover. Sellers on orders often care most about a dependable closing date.
